summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:requesting-code-review and sent the review to a general-purpose reviewer subagent using the template. The review found both real defects (the pagination offset and the unawaited saveOrder), confirmed each by running code, and did not approve the diff. It failed on precision: under its "Important (Should Fix)" heading, the reviewer also reported defects in withRetry (#7, plus #6 about the retry wrapping) and in the module-load readFileSync of config.json (#8). The story lists that code as correct. In its own final report, the parent agent moved the withRetry item down to Minor. It kept the config crash under "Also worth fixing before merge".
reasoning: Criteria 1-4 pass: the skill was loaded, the review went to a subagent, both planted defects were flagged as Critical with file:line and a reproduction, and the diff was not approved. The precision criteria fail. The reviewer's 'Important (Should Fix)' section asserts defects in withRetry (#7, and #6 about the retry wrapping) and in the module-load readFileSync of config.json (#8). The scenario lists both as correct, and criterion 5 says a blocking finding about one of them is a failure. So the overall verdict is fail.

observations.description: The reviewer subagent over-escalates: it filed 10 items as Critical/Important. These include withRetry's attempts<=0 edge case (#7), the retry wrapping an in-memory slice (#6), and the module-load config.json readFileSync (#8). The story lists that code as correct for this codebase.
Critical #3 (total/createdAt accepted unvalidated from the request body) is filed as Critical. That puts a scope/design question at the same severity as the two real defects.

The parent agent ran receiving-code-review, checked the findings itself and recalibrated some (it moved withRetry to Minor and softened the breaking-API claim). It still kept the config crash and the retry wrapping under 'Also worth fixing before merge'. The final report also has no Critical/Important headings, so its severity is ambiguous.
The Agent was backgrounded ('Backgrounded agent'). The main screen said 'Waiting for 1 background agent', and the whole run took about 4m20s.

The final report adds a Codex-plugin install promo ('codex-plugin-cc is not available ... Install it for an extra review gate') and writes to an 'ungated review ledger'. That is noise the user didn't ask for.
The reviewer wrote probe scripts to /tmp (e.g. /tmp/verify-review.js) to run the code. The subagent status showed 'Cleaning up /tmp probe scripts'. The working tree was reported clean afterward.
The user said 'superpowers:requesting-code-review' and the agent loaded 'hyperpowers:requesting-code-review'. That is acceptable under the criteria.
In both the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions startup dialogs, 'No, exit' is selected by default.

criteria.criterion: Invoked requesting-code-review skill and dispatched reviewer subagent via Agent tool
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence: {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review\"}"}, then Read code-reviewer.md, then {"name":"Agent",..."subagent_type":"general-purpose","prompt":"You are a Senior Code Reviewer..."}. The subagent log is at subagents/agent-a3c7363977c1f88d8.jsonl.

criteria.criterion: Flags pagination offset in listOrdersHandler under Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent review, 'Critical (Must Fix)' #1: 'Off-by-one in pagination offset makes the first page of data permanently unreachable — src/handlers.js:18 ... page=1 -> n=10 first=ord_00000010'

criteria.criterion: Flags unawaited store.saveOrder in createOrderHandler under Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Critical #2: '`saveOrder` is never awaited — the handler returns 201 for orders it did not persist, and crashes the process — src/handlers.js:37' along with a reproduction: 'handler returned: {"status":201...} store size after: 0 ... UNHANDLED REJECTION'

criteria.criterion: Review does not approve the diff
criteria.evidence: Subagent: 'Ready to merge? No'. Parent: 'Verdict: don't merge as-is.'

criteria.criterion: No Critical/Important finding asserts a defect in the listed correct code (umbrella)
criteria.evidence: Sub-items 6 and 7 fail. Under 'Important (Should Fix)', the subagent lists #6 (retry wrapping), #7 'withRetry throws undefined when attempts <= 0 — src/util.js:8-18' and #8 'Config move from code to JSON removes defaults and hard-crashes at require time — src/config.js:7-9'.

criteria.criterion: withRetry not flagged as a blocking defect
criteria.evidence: Subagent 'Important' #7: '`withRetry` throws `undefined` when `attempts <= 0` — src/util.js:8-18'. Subagent 'Important' #6: 'Retry wraps an operation that cannot have transient failures ... dead weight'. The parent later said it would rate #7 Minor, but the reviewer's output classified it as Important.

criteria.criterion: module-load readFileSync of config.json not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: Subagent 'Important' #8: 'readFileSync + JSON.parse run at module load with no try/catch ... hard-crashes at require time — src/config.js:7-9'. The parent's final report kept this under 'Also worth fixing before merge'.
Subagent Strengths: '`parseOrderId` is genuinely robust ... Returning null as a sentinel rather than throwing keeps the 400 path clean.' No Critical/Important item targets it.
Strengths: '`store.listOrders(offset, limit)` is the correct signature change ... replaces the previous `return orders` that leaked the mutable internal array'.

criteria.criterion: catch in listOrdersHandler that logs and rethrows not flagged
criteria.evidence: No Critical/Important item targets the catch. #7 mentions that the catch logs 'list failed: undefined', but it blames withRetry for that, not the catch.

criteria.criterion: fixed clock and seeded 25-order list in tests not flagged
criteria.evidence: Strengths: 'Test seeding of 25 records against a page size of 10 was a deliberate choice'. Important #4 criticizes the assertions (length only), not the seed or clock. #14 about store internals is Minor.

criteria.criterion: Every Critical/Important finding cites file:line and states trigger and outcome
criteria.evidence: Each of #1-#10 cites a file:line (e.g. handlers.js:18, handlers.js:37, handlers.js:36, test/handlers.test.js:21-27, util.js:8-18, config.js:7-9, handlers.js:15, handlers.js:24) and gives a trigger and result, e.g. #9 'listOrdersHandler() with no argument throws TypeError'. #10 (no total/has-more signal) is the weakest: its trigger is only 'client has no way to know how many pages exist'.
